strategy.summary: Reproduce scipy issue 21058 by building scipy at buggy commit b3cf42e98594 with the documented build pins and running the PR's added test_pro_rad1, which compares scipy.special.pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1) to WolframAlpha values at rtol 2e-5. On the buggy revision the first return value is about -93126.77 instead of about 0.00966, so the test fails; on the fixed revision the values match and it passes. Scipy's numpy and python-version constraints are era-inferred, so numpy 1.26.4 on Python 3.12 is chosen to match the reporter.

system_packages: gfortran (gcc 13.x family, as the reporter used gfortran from gcc 13.3.0)
a C and C++ compiler (clang 15 as on the reporter's macOS build, or gcc on Linux)
BLAS/LAPACK backend: OpenBLAS on Linux (reporter's Linux backend not stated); Apple Accelerate only if reproducing on macOS arm64
build_commands: git checkout b3cf42e98594 && git submodule update --init
pinned_because: pybind11 2.12.0 is a documented build dependency in issue 21058 build info, so it is pinned
cython 3.0.10 is a documented compiler constraint in issue 21058, so it is pinned
pythran 0.16.1 is a documented compiler constraint in issue 21058, so it is pinned
numpy 1.26.4 is the reporter's version; no documented constraint exists, so it is chosen to match the reporter, and it is era-inferred rather than documented
scipy version is not pinned separately; the test runs from the checked-out buggy commit, since the 1.14.0 release is only the reporter's version label
pyyaml is not installed: the issue only shows a warning suggesting it, which is not a stated requirement

strategy.reproducing_test: scipy/special/tests/test_specfun.py::test_pro_rad1, which calls special.pro_rad1(1, 1, 30, 1.1) and asserts assert_allclose(res, (0.009657872296166435, 3.253369651472877), rtol=2e-5)
strategy.success_criterion: On buggy b3cf42e98594 the test FAILS: assert_allclose reports a mismatch because the first component is about -93126.77 against an expected about 0.009658. On the fixed revision (the PR head containing the sphj index and argument-order fixes) the test PASSES because both components agree with the expected values within rtol 2e-5. The transition is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: python3 -c "from scipy import special; print(special.pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1))" should print a value near (-93126.77, 2390688.11) on the buggy build and near (0.0096578, 3.25337) on the fixed build
risks: The transition depends on the algorithm (wrong dj index and swapped sphj arguments), not on the platform. The buggy error is gross, so any backend should show it, but this is inferred from the algorithm and not confirmed on Linux.

The reporter's macOS arm64 build used Apple Accelerate, and the Linux reporter's backend is not stated. If the behaviour were backend-dependent, a plan on OpenBLAS could fail to transition; this is unverified.

The PR diff also changes msta2 to return nn + 10. That change is unexplained and is not assumed to be part of the fix. If the fixed revision's test depends on it, the transition could be caused by more than sphj.

The test tolerance was bumped for linux 32bit in a commit with an unstated value. The 64-bit run at rtol 2e-5 is expected to be unaffected, because the buggy error is far larger than any tolerance, but 32-bit behaviour is not verified.
The commit b3cf42e98594 is a main-branch snapshot, not the 1.14.0 release the reporter used. Confirm that the buggy commit reproduces the wrong values before relying on the transition.
The numpy version is chosen rather than documented. If the build fails with numpy 1.26.4 at this commit, a different numpy within the era range would be needed.
The numerically_relevant flag for numpy is recorded as false in the environment but true in the dependency constraints. The plan treats numpy as an unconstrained, unverified choice either way.

oracle.reference_source: WolframAlpha/Mathematica SpheroidalS1 and SpheroidalS1Prime values in the test comment
oracle.why: The reference values are rounded and the test compares against them at rtol 2e-5, so the oracle is a tolerance comparison rather than exact equality

strategy.fails_on_buggy: On b3cf42e98594 pro_rad1(1,1,30,1.1) returns (-93126.77, 2390688.11). assert_allclose compares this against (0.00965787, 3.25337) at rtol 2e-5, so the first element mismatches by many orders of magnitude and the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: On the fixed revision the output is about (0.0096578, 3.25334). Both relative differences from the test's expected values are about 8e-6, within rtol 2e-5, so the test passes.
